articles.title: Syrian Archbishop Safe After Armed Robbery As Patriarchs Warn Of Violence Against Christians
articles.content:
by Stefan J. Bos, Worthy News Chief International Correspondent

HOMS, SYRIA (Worthy News) – A Melkite Greek Catholic archbishop in Syria says he is safe after assailants bound, blindfolded and gagged him during an armed robbery at his office in Homs. Three Syrian patriarchs condemned the attack and urged authorities to address a series of assaults and kidnappings they say have particularly affected Christians.

The Melkite Greek Catholic Archdiocese of Homs confirmed that armed robbers entered its premises on Saturday, November 14, while Archbishop Jean-Abdo Arbach was inside. In a joint statement Tuesday, the patriarchs said the assailants tied up Arbach, covered his eyes and gagged him before stealing items from his office.

Arbach told the Catholic charity Aid to the Church in Need (ACN) by telephone on Tuesday that he was safe. He thanked God for coming through the ordeal and expressed gratitude for the prayers and messages of solidarity he had received, the charity reported Wednesday.

ACN said the robbers ransacked the office and took several personal belongings, including an image of the Virgin Mary. The Syrian Observatory for Human Rights reported that they also took a safe and the cross Arbach was wearing.

PATRIARCHS URGE ACTION

Arbach told ACN that the investigation was ongoing and that he would wait for the circumstances to be clarified before commenting further. As of Thursday, authorities had yet to announce any arrests or publicly establish a motive.

Melkite Greek Catholic Patriarch Youssef I Absi, Greek Orthodox Patriarch John X and Syriac Orthodox Patriarch Ignatius Aphrem II urged Syrian authorities to investigate the attacks, make their findings public and take steps to protect citizens.

The patriarchs warned that repeated assaults and kidnappings were raising questions about the future of Christians in Syria. They cited the kidnapping for ransom of a jeweler in Al-Suqaylabiyah, a predominantly Christian town in western Hama province, and reaffirmed their commitment to peaceful coexistence between Christians and Muslims based on equal citizenship.

The town also saw outbreaks of violence in March and October. In March, men on motorcycles from a neighboring town attacked Christian-owned property after a local dispute. A United Nations briefing cited reports that unidentified gunmen on motorcycles opened fire at shops and civilians on October 3, prompting protests by local Christians and a response from security forces.

CALL FOR RECONCILIATION

ACN Executive President Regina Lynch called Arbach “a courageous shepherd who has remained close to his people throughout so many years of war and suffering.” She expressed solidarity with the archbishop and with Syrians who continue to live in fear.

Arbach has worked with ACN for years to draw attention to the needs of Syrians affected by war. The charity has helped fund emergency aid, education and medical care in the Homs region, as well as the rebuilding of homes and churches.

In March 2025, after a wave of violence in western Syria, Arbach told ACN, “We don’t want any more bloodshed. We call for unity and reconciliation.” He also highlighted the Church’s efforts to provide food, medicine, accommodation and spiritual support to Christian families.

Following the robbery, Lynch said ACN backed the Syrian Church leaders’ appeal for authorities to protect all citizens and work toward lasting peace.

The post Syrian Archbishop Safe After Armed Robbery As Patriarchs Warn Of Violence Against Christians appeared first on Worthy Christian News.

articles.title: Can you go to nursing school without getting vaccinated? Yes, but only in Indiana!
articles.content:
Executive summary

One of my readers asked an interesting question about vaccines and nursing school:

Hello Mr. Kirsch,

Our youngest daughter is considering nursing school. Is there any school in the U.S. that does not require the vaccine, or will give an exemption for it?

We learned that the choice of words matter, such that a school that has mandatory vaccines/requires them might “unrequire them” for reasons within a defined parameter.

What does this mean for potential MD students who also don’t want to get that vaccine? Are we shutting a sector of society out of those fields?

It turns out there are schools that don’t require the COVID shots, but only in Indiana, can you totally escape vaccination requirements for all vaccines, starting July 1, 2026.

Indiana passed a law requiring religious exemptions be respected, but it applied only to the schools, and not the clinics required to complete your training. On March 12, 2026, they closed the loophole to apply also to the clinics.

Full AlterAI AI analysis here.

Here’s the picture in other states: you can get out of the COVID shots, but not the other shots

What’s amazing is if you have high titers, you can escape the shots in many places. A pleasant surprise for sure!

🟢 Schools With an Explicit COVID Exemption Process (Medical and/or Religious)

These are programs that publish a real process — not a promise of placement.

  • UT Arlington (TX) — College of Nursing considers medical and religious exemptions case by case; COVID not required by the university itself. Hospital sites generally accept COVID and flu exemptions. Exemption applies only inside the school; clinical site decides separately.

  • Standard College of Nursing (Falls Church, VA) — COVID religious exemption, renewed annually, requires personal statement plus a statement from your religious leader. Moral, philosophical, and conscientious objection explicitly rejected.

  • Xavier University (Cincinnati, OH) — medical and religious exemption through the university, but the nursing college warns your compliance portal will stay flagged as rejected all program long, and you must re-seek approval every semester and at every new clinical facility.

  • Milligan University (TN) — medical exemption and religious exception, with the honesty that some affiliated sites won’t accept either.

  • Butler Community College (KS) — COVID exemption/declination with either provider documentation or a letter explaining religious belief, plus a flu declination form with stated reasons.

  • McLennan Community College (TX) — exemptions for both annual flu and COVID on medical or conscience grounds, reviewed by program director and dean. Not guaranteed, and sites can refuse.

  • Barnes-Jewish College Goldfarb School of Nursing (St. Louis) — separate religious and medical exemption forms for both COVID and influenza.

  • Thiel College (PA) — religious or medical exemption through student health for health-care programs.

  • Liberty University (VA) — university-level medical and religious exemption forms; nursing clinical prerequisites still run through the partner sites.

  • Grand Canyon University (AZ) — university-level medical, religious, and personal exemptions; nursing rotations subject to each facility.

  • Chamberlain University — immunization waiver request exists, but the school states plainly the exemption only covers Chamberlain’s own policy, not the facility’s.

  • University of Kansas Medical Center — COVID religious and medical exemption forms, though some partner sites refuse religious exemptions outright and force a leave of absence instead.

  • Ramapo College (NJ) — granted a nursing student’s religious exemption, then allegedly told her security would be called if she entered the building. She withdrew and sued.

🟡 Schools That Don’t Require COVID at All

Better odds than any exemption form — the school has nothing to exempt you from.

  • Northeastern Junior College (CO)

  • CSU San Marcos and CSU Fullerton (CA)

  • University of Kansas Medical Center

  • Northwest Mississippi Community College

  • Miami Dade College (FL)

  • Azusa Pacific University (CA)

  • Southern Regional Technical College (GA)

  • Sampson Community College (NC)

  • New Jersey City University

  • University of Arizona College of Nursing

  • Texas A&M College of Nursing — COVID absent from its current compliance list; flu is required annually

  • North Central Technical College (WI) LVN — notes the DFW Hospital Council standards allow flu exemption for medical or religious reasons

🔵 Schools With Explicit Flu Exemption Processes

  • Conemaugh School of Nursing (PA) — medical and religious flu exemptions; no approved exemption by deadline means no clinical.

  • Lamar University (TX) — medical or religious flu exemption; masking required, and if no site accepts you, you withdraw from the course.

  • Tennessee Tech (TN) — medical exception and religious accommodation forms for flu.

  • University of Pittsburgh School of Nursing — medical and religious flu exemption request form.

  • Walden University — flu declination form or provider-signed waiver.

  • Barnes-Jewish, McLennan, Butler CC — as above, both vaccines.

  • Western Massachusetts clinical consortium — Baystate and Cooley Dickinson accept school-approved medical or religious flu exemptions; Holyoke and Mercy accept declination.

  • Mt. SAC’s hospital list (CA) — Adventist Health White Memorial, BHC-Alhambra, Chino, Corona Regional, Pomona Valley, St. Jude, and the Silverado facilities all allow COVID declination or exemption; several also allow flu declination.

🔴 Schools That Refuse Religious Exemptions or Refuse All Exemptions

Know these before you waste an application fee.

  • Washington State University College of Nursing — medical exemptions only. “The CON cannot accept religious exemptions.” Also: “There are no exemptions for TB screening.”

  • Dordt University (IA) — no religious exemption for nursing students at all, because it would block clinical progression.

  • Ponce Health Sciences University (PR) — “No exemptions will be permitted in the Medical or Nursing programs.”

  • Wayne State University College of Nursing (MI) — “No exemptions from the vaccination requirements are allowed, including... medical or religious reasons,” except documented life-threatening anaphylaxis.

  • NYU Rory Meyers — religious exemption exists on paper but is curtailed by NYS Department of Health rules for anyone entering covered health care facilities.

  • Truckee Meadows Community College CNA (NV) — “mandatory, no exceptions and no exemptions.”

  • EVIT practical nursing (AZ) — “EXEMPTIONS for any reason are not accepted.”

  • Collin College (TX) and McLennan — no exemption process for the state-mandated list (Tdap, MMR, Hep B, varicella).

⚫ What’s Mandated With Effectively No Exemption

These are the walls. Note that almost all of them can be satisfied by a positive titer rather than a shot — which is the actual escape hatch most people miss.

Requirement

Exemption reality

MMR

Universal. Titer accepted nearly everywhere; no religious exemption at clinical sites

Hepatitis B

Universal, with post-series surface antibody titer. A handful of Texas schools accept a provider-written waiver; most do not

Varicella

Universal. Positive titer or two doses; history of chickenpox usually rejected without labs

Tdap

Universal. No titer exists, so there is no way to test out — this is the one with genuinely no alternative

TB screening

Not a vaccine, but a hard gate. WSU: no exemptions, period. Annual or two-step baseline at most programs

Influenza

Annual. Exemptible at many schools, zero-exemption at some sites — San Antonio Regional mandates it with no exemptions; College Hospital accepts only egg allergy

COVID

Widely variable; some hospitals still refuse all exemptions (Hillcrest Woods, Huntington on the Mt. SAC list)

🧭 How to Actually Work This

State law is your leverage, and it’s uneven. Texas statute (TAC 97.62 and 97.64) permits exclusion from compliance for medical contraindications and reasons of conscience, including religious belief — a notarized DSHS affidavit, valid two years, explicitly covering students in health-related courses. But schools like McLennan read the clinical-site rule as overriding it. Utah law requires colleges to offer medical and personal exemptions, but carves out students in medical settings entirely.

Ask three questions before you pay a deposit:

  1. “Give me the current list of clinical affiliates and which ones accept school-approved exemptions.” If they won’t produce it in writing, that’s your answer.

  2. “Is the exemption granted by the school, or does each site re-review it?” Xavier and UTA both re-review every semester.

  3. “What happens to my tuition and progression if no site accepts me?” Most handbooks say: withdrawal, no refund, program incomplete.

And understand what the “religious” test is actually doing. Schools demanding a pastor’s letter, published denominational doctrine, or a notarized statement aren’t verifying sincerity — they’re running a filter designed to wash out anyone without institutional religious cover. A private individual with a genuine conviction and no congregation is exactly who those forms are built to exclude.

Summary

The vaccinated v. unvaccinated studies published in the scientific literature all show people with fewer vaccines are healthier. No exceptions.

Yet to get through nursing school today, except for Indiana, you have to sacrifice your health.

Isn’t it amazing how religious exemptions are safe in Indiana, but unsafe in other states?

This explains why so many nurses are pro-vax: the schools simply don’t accept those with critical thinking skills.

Share

articles.title: A single pull request could have handed attackers the keys to Microsoft’s software supply chain
articles.content:
A now patched vulnerability in WinGet's moderation tooling could have handed attackers a Microsoft employee's GitHub credentials through a single pull request.

The most dangerous actor in a software supply chain may now be an automated script with powerful credentials and no idea where it’s sending them.

Researchers from pen-testing company Cycode have discovered a now patched critical zero-click supply chain vulnerability in the open-source Windows Package Manager (WinGet), which sits on billions of devices worldwide.

A single pull request could have tricked Microsoft’s internal tooling into freely handing over a moderator’s GitHub access token, with no phishing, no malware, no moderator clicking or approval required.

There is currently no evidence that the flaw has been exploited in the wild. But it serves as a cautionary tale for enterprises that the automation they trust is becoming an attacker entry point, and package repositories are particularly enticing targets.

“Package registries have become the highest-profile target in the software supply chain,” Moriel Harush, Cycode security research lead, wrote in a blog post. “Compromise a single maintainer, and you reach everyone who trusts them. Compromise the gatekeepers, and you reach the entire ecosystem.”

Whatever the employee can do, the attacker can do

WinGet is Microsoft’s free, open source command line tool that helps users discover, install, upgrade, configure, and remove apps. It exists on more than 1.4 billion active devices running Windows 10, Windows 11, and Windows Server 2025.

WinGet’s catalog is a public GitHub repository, and its gatekeeper, so to speak, is a small, official group of Microsoft moderators who review a constant stream of community pull requests and proposed changes. By default, WinGet installations on every Windows machine trust the actions those keepers take.

The hole is in the moderators’ own internal triage tool. This PowerShell helper attached the moderator’s secret GitHub Personal Access Token (PAT) to any HTTP request, without checking who owned that address.

This meant an attacker merely had to supply an address. Theoretically, if they opened a pull request and pointed an InstallerURL software installation package at their own server, “the trap was set,” Harush explained.

Microsoft’s automated Azure DevOps validation pipeline would then attempt to fetch the URL, but the attacker’s server would intentionally return an error. This added a validation error label to the pull request.

The moderator’s internal script would respond to that label by running a CheckInstaller routine which would send a HEAD request to the attacker via an authenticated HTTP helper, whose job is to automatically attach credentials or tokens to outgoing HTTP requests and handle authorization errors. Then all the attacker had to do was check their logs and extract the moderator’s official GitHub token, which was “casually” handed over.

But the token is not merely a repository-scoped credential, it is a full identity credential, meaning whatever that Microsoft employee can do on GitHub, the token can do.

Harush explained: “It is like a courier stapling your house key to every parcel that has your name on it, because most of them are destined for your own address.” But if a stranger uses your name and changes the address to one they control, “your key is delivered directly to them.”

Armed with this key to Microsoft’s internal environment, an attacker could push malicious manifests, approve their own pull requests, and slip in backdoored installers to 14,000 exposed packages, all under a highly trusted, official Microsoft badge.

They could also access and write to every other Microsoft repository the moderator had access to, modify GitHub Actions workflows across those repositories to achieve remote code execution (RCE) and exfiltrate corporate secrets.

There is a precondition for this attack: At least one moderator has to have the triage tracker running in a continuous background loop, which it is designed to do as it waits for work.

Underlying model ‘fundamentally flawed’

Harush pointed out that Microsoft’s C# version of the tool, in the same directory, did not share the flaw; as such, it would have offered safer authentication. Microsoft has since patched the PowerShell vulnerability, safely scoping the authentication mechanism to ensure that users’ tokens are only attached when a request host is an authorized GitHub endpoint, such as api.github.com, github.com, or raw.githubusercontent.com.

Harush noted, however, that the underlying credential model is “fundamentally flawed,” and that relying on Classic PATs is a “severe liability.”

Cycode advises binding credentials to destinations, rather than functions; auditing every internal tool that handles maintainer credentials; and ensuring that headers are conditionally applied based on the target host, “not unconditionally stapled by a wrapper function.” Treat all user inputs as hostile, validated hosts before credentials are attached, and deprecate classic PATs.

“The blast radius of a leaked token must be limited to one repository and the bare minimum permissions,” Harush said. “A leaked token should never mean a leaked corporate identity.”

He emphasized, though, that WinGet moderators are doing exactly what’s asked of them: Using automated tools to manage a “flood of community submissions” and make their jobs easier. “But automation does not just remove the human who would have clicked the malicious link; it removes the human who would have noticed the anomaly.”

Scripts are a soft spot

The WinGet flaw was a near miss, but “a very serious one,” said Frank Dickson of Dickson Research. Exploiting it would have let an attacker publish malware with “Microsoft’s seal of approval.”

This means attackers could have pushed tampered installers to anyone who ran an install or an update, reached into any other Microsoft repositories the moderator could touch, and hijacked the build machinery to steal more secrets.

And the damage would have looked like routine work. An IT team scripting a standard software rollout would have installed the attacker’s code on every machine, and the logs would have shown an approved package from an approved source.

“The attack would have been a Trojan horse delivered by the mail carrier everyone trusts,” Dickson said.

Enterprise security teams should learn that their own scripts are a soft spot, he pointed out; internal tools, bots, and automation get production-level keys and hobby-level review. CISOs should inventory every script and bot that holds a token, and answer important questions: What could this key do in the wrong hands? Where is it allowed to go?

Additionally, he advised replacing broad, long-lived tokens with narrow, short-lived ones, and binding every credential to the specific services that need it, which is exactly how Microsoft fixed this problem. “Also, enterprises should stop trusting public registries blindly,” Dickson said.

Ultimately, security teams should review their automations the way they review their people, he said. “A script that runs in a loop around the clock with a moderator’s keys is, in effect, a moderator who never sleeps and never questions anything.”

articles.title: European Commission HR hit by cyber attack
articles.content:
Shortly after the FBI warned about risks from open source AI tool ARTEX, the Commission confirmed that attackers used it to try to access personnel records.

Barely a week after the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) warned companies of the cyber attacker interest in an open source penetration testing tool called ARTEX, the European Commission has confirmed that attackers armed with that tool broke into its HR systems.

The attack, which Commission officials detected on October 22, forced them to shut off much of the access to the systems for more than 10 days.

“As a protective and preventive measure, we temporarily took down several applications and most of them have since then been restored,” Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier said Thursday. “We have not detected any evidence of a data breach affecting Commission staff as a whole.”

During a news media briefing, a transcript of which was provided to CSOonline, he said that the European Data Protection Supervisor (EDPS) was informed of the attack, “so there was no hiding whatsoever.”

Regnier would not go into detail about the attacks, given that the matter is still being investigated, but he did say, “it is a campaign, so there was a series of incidents.”

In an email, Commission officials added, “we are also preventively checking other systems while staying in close contact with CERT-EU and the EDPS.”

ARTEX popular with attackers

The November 13 FBI statement about ARTEX, described as an autonomous penetration testing framework, said that the tool is becoming very popular with attackers.

“Since at least August 2026, a variety of malicious cyber actors have used ARTEX to conduct campaigns targeting organizations globally across multiple sectors, including financial services, government, technology, defense, semiconductor, energy, healthcare, manufacturing, telecommunications, and legal industries,” the FBI advisory said. “ARTEX significantly reduces the time required to chain attack techniques, with some intrusions progressing from initial targeting to privileged access in under three hours. The framework enables threat actors with minimal technical expertise to conduct complex, multi-target operations simultaneously, fundamentally accelerating attack velocity and expanding operational scale.”

Although ARTEX can handle a wide range of pentesting functions, it appeared to be primarily used in the Commission attack to search for and locate credentials.

The FBI said that ARTEX can “automatically map effective permissions of Azure credentials–SAS tokens, Service Principals, Kudu credentials, Storage Account keys–using sub-second capability checks.”

ARTEX has been known to SOC operations since GitHub first released the tool in July, but widespread misuse of the tool prompted GitHub to make it unavailable on October 8. “Despite this action, ARTEX remains widely accessible through independent routes and mirrors on code-sharing platforms,” the FBI said.

Uses different tactics

Brian Levine, a partner with consulting firm Control Risks, added that ARTEX’s AI-fueled tactics are different from what many cybersecurity teams are used to.

“ARTEX doesn’t need to steal your keys. It finds the ones you left lying around, like a SAS token in a code repo, a storage key in a config file, or a Kudu credential nobody rotated. Then it tries each one against every door in under a second,” he said. “Picture a burglar walking the block at 3 a.m. and checking every car door handle. He isn’t breaking glass. He’s taking inventory of what you left unlocked and AI lets him work a thousand blocks at once.”

Companies need a secure fallback

Noah Kenney, principal consultant at Digital 520, said he was unimpressed with the Commission’s attempts to tell EU citizens that all was well.

“The Commission says it has no evidence of a breach affecting its staff ‘as a whole,’ which is very different from saying that there is no evidence of a breach affecting any of the staff,” Kenney said. “The wording doesn’t give me much comfort.”

Kenney also said that the attackers’ decision to target HR was not an accident, and that the Commission’s decision to temporarily shut down some systems may have inadvertently helped the intruders.

“When payroll, leave, and medical reimbursement systems go down, people start using spreadsheets, email and manual approvals. Those workarounds often have weaker access controls and worse audit trails than the systems taken offline,” he said. “Enterprises need to define a secure fallback process before the attack, because improvising one often leads to greater exposure.”

HR systems a prize

Levine also said that the choice of an HR victim was understandable.

“HR systems are a prize. Names, home addresses, pay grades and health insurance records for EU civil servants make a ready-made targeting list for espionage and social engineering,” he said. “Whether or not data left the building, every Commission employee should prepare to receive a very convincing phishing email soon.”

His advice to CISOs: “Get secrets out of code and pipelines and rotate anything that has been exposed. Give every token and service principal only the access it needs, so a found key opens a closet, not the vault. Put cloud admin interfaces behind private access.”

articles.title: Malaysian military to enlist gamers to strengthen its drone capabilities
articles.content:
KUALA LUMPUR – The Armed Forces are looking at tapping into the digital skills of the nation’s youth, including gamers, to strengthen its drone capabilities, says Jeneral Tan Sri Malek Razak Sulaiman.

The Armed Forces chief stressed however that experience in video games alone would not qualify someone to become a military drone operator.

Malek Razak said the military is continuously monitoring developments in defence technology and identifying the expertise required to support the operation of unmanned aerial systems (UAS), particularly for intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) missions in the South China Sea.

“The increasing sophistication of military technology requires specialised knowledge and skills, including technical expertise, operational coordination and the ability to make sound decisions under challenging conditions,” he said in an interview recently.

Malaysia bought three ANKA-S units for RM423.8mil earlier this year and plans to buy three more in a second phase as it expands its intelligence gathering and unmanned surveillance capabilities in the South China Sea and waters off Sabah.

While experience in video games or recreational drone operations could be considered an added advantage, Malek Razak said these did not automatically translate into the competencies required for military operations.

“Operating military drones involves specialised training, technical knowledge, an understanding of operational procedures, discipline and the ability to carry out missions safely.

While experience in video games or recreational drone operations could be considered an added advantage, Malek Razak said these did not automatically translate into the competencies required for military operations.

“Operating military drones involves specialised training, technical knowledge, an understanding of operational procedures, discipline and the ability to carry out missions safely.

“An individual must possess comprehensive knowledge of the system, understand flight safety, risk management, operational procedures and responsibilities when carrying out missions,” he said.

Recruitment and selection would continue to be based on established qualifications, aptitude and competency assessments, he added.

“Digital technology and changing interests among the younger generation had created opportunities to identify potential talent for the military,” he said.

Malek Razak said the military is open to exploring creative and innovative approaches to attract young Malaysians, including the use of digital platforms, interactive technology, simulations and activities based on skills.

“These could serve as effective platforms to introduce military capabilities, including unmanned systems, communications, cybersecurity and modern defence technology.

“However, such approaches must not compromise the ­standards of discipline, professionalism and responsibility expected of military personnel,” he said.

On recruitment, Malek Razak said the military is continuously reviewing its intake policies to ensure that personnel development remains relevant to technological advancements and changing security requirements.

“The expansion of Skim Perkhidmatan Askar Lasykar Angkatan Tetap (Permanent Commissioned Officers Scheme) from Jan 1 this year, had widened academic and career opportunities for eligible personnel.

“The initiative included broader access to Skim Tauliah Pegawai Tetap (Regular Commissioned Officers Scheme) and the Special Service List category,” he said.

The Armed Forces had also opened recruitment opportunities to holders of Vocational Education and Training (TVET) qualifications, including the Malaysian Skills Certificate (SKM) and Malaysian Skills Diploma (DKM) (Level 2 and 3), as well as qualifications from the National Dual Training System (SLDN), he added.

“The move would help broaden the recruitment pool, particularly among young people with relevant technical skills,” he said.

articles.title: Mending Japan-China ties looks to be a long battle; President Xi briefly civil to PM Takaichi at APEC summit
articles.content:
SHENZHEN – Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Chinese President Xi Jinping shook hands on Wednesday, but everything else in their brief interaction suggested that repairing strained bilateral ties might not happen anytime soon.

Ahead of a dinner reception, Xi individually greeted and posed for photos with all the leaders who have assembled for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen. Xi wore a relatively gentle expression as he greeted Takaichi, but he made eye contact only briefly before turning away. Xi did not appear to reply after Takaichi spoke to him with a smile as they shook hands.

Earlier in the day, Takaichi had been greeted at the airport by Zhang Qiyue, a protocol ambassador for China’s Foreign Ministry. The welcome was completely different to that afforded to U.S. President Donald Trump, who was met by Xi himself on the tarmac, and Russian President Vladimir Putin, who was greeted by Cai Qi, a member of the Politburo Standing Committee and the fifth-ranked figure in the Chinese Communist Party.

Leaders of other important nations disembarked to a large number of dancers, but the welcome for Takaichi was strikingly no-frills and muted.

Split views within govt

Takaichi and Xi held their first in-person talks on the sidelines of the APEC summit meeting held in South Korea in October 2025, where the leaders agreed they would promote a “mutually beneficial relationship based on common strategic interests.” However, bilateral ties deteriorated rapidly from the following month, after Takaichi’s Diet remark regarding a Taiwan contingency. Officials within the Japanese government have been split over how to approach the first opportunity for contact between the two leaders since then, with proactive and cautious views remaining at odds until the last minute.

“Even if holding a formal meeting will be difficult, progress can be made even during talks on the sidelines,” a senior official at the Prime Minister’s Office said to The Yomiuri Shimbun. “We should actively reach out to the other side.”

The official even suggested the government should consider urging Trump to help set up a meeting.

With Xi increasingly concentrating authority in his own hands, holding direct talks with the Chinese leader could hold the key to resolving the situation. Xi, who appears determined to reunify Taiwan with mainland China, was reportedly furious at Takaichi’s remark in the Diet. Many government officials therefore preferred a softly-softly approach to arranging talks, fearing that carelessly rushing in “could end up being counterproductive.”

A source close to Takaichi admitted that it was unclear even as late as Tuesday how Takaichi would approach Xi. “That was left up to the prime minister to decide,” the source said. As Takaichi extended her hand to shake Xi’s at Wednesday’s event, she said what appeared to be a message that had been prepared in advance. However, Xi’s apparent lack of reaction signified there was no change in his position.

Takaichi will seek reelection as Liberal Democratic Party president next autumn. It will become even more difficult for her to make concessions, such as retracting her Diet remark, that could spark a backlash from conservative members of the ruling party. Former Prime Minister Yasuo Fukuda, who was trusted by former Prime Minister Shinzo Abe — a key political mentor of Takaichi — to improve diplomatic relations with Beijing, died last month, which has further narrowed the prime minister’s available channels of communication with China.

“Improving ties could take several years,” a Japanese Foreign Ministry insider said, sharing a pessimistic view that has been spreading within the government. For the time being, the government likely will continue to focus on strengthening relations with the United States and other like-minded countries.

People-to-people exchanges

The Chinese side viewed Takaichi’s remark as hinting at “military intervention” in the Taiwan issue and has stuck to its position of demanding a retraction and correction. Beijing also appears set to continue applying economic pressure through steps including restrictions on rare earth exports, and criticizing the bolstering of Japan’s defense capabilities as a “new militarism.” Despite this, people-to-people and economic exchanges are still forging ahead, apparently unaffected by the words being lobbed between the two governments.

A delegation from the Japan Association for the Promotion of International Trade, which is headed by former Foreign Minister Takeshi Iwaya, visited China in September, and an economic organization from the Kansai region plans to visit China in December and hold talks with high-ranking Chinese government officials in Beijing.

The Xi administration is preparing for the Chinese Communist Party’s national congress, scheduled to be held in the latter half of 2027. Although Xi has incentive to maintain stability in China’s diplomatic relations, he can little afford to adopt a posture that could be perceived as showing weakness toward Japan. An approach that combines carrots and sticks likely will keep rattling the Takaichi administration in the months ahead.

articles.title: Security stepped up amid fears of fresh unrest in Bangladesh
articles.content:
DHAKA – Security has been tightened across the country following a series of crude bomb explosions and arson attacks in at least 21 districts this month, amid intelligence warnings of further unrest ahead of December.

Intelligence sources said activists of the Awami League, whose activities are banned, its affiliated organisations and the banned Chhatra League may attempt to destabilise the country over former prime minister Sheikh Hasina’s announced return in December.

Interrogations of arrested suspects and analyses of mobile phone conversations and messages suggest possible plans to disrupt road, rail and waterway communications, isolate Gopalganj and neighbouring districts, and organise large gatherings in Dhaka, officials said.

Police data show 70 crude bomb explosions and arson attacks on 57 vehicles between November 7 and 17. During this period, 35 cases were filed and 60 people arrested. A police vehicle was damaged in a crude bomb explosion, while two police establishments came under attack. Police also reported 528 arrests between November 1 and 17 over alleged involvement in political instability.

Gopalganj witnessed some of the worst violence. Violence was also reported in Dhaka, Chattogram, Natore, Khulna, Faridpur, Barguna, Manikganj, Naogaon, Kishoreganj, Shariatpur, Madaripur, Rajshahi and Kurigram, among other districts. Gazipur, Mymensingh, Netrokona, Kushtia, Jhenaidah, Pirojpur, Bagerhat and Barishal are also considered vulnerable.

Following the violence, Inspector General of Police Md Ali Hossain Fakir instructed police in border districts to step up surveillance to prevent the infiltration of weapons, explosives and suspected individuals.

Intelligence agencies are also examining mobile financial transactions of arrested suspects to trace funding sources.

A senior Police Headquarters official said, “It is difficult to bring the situation under control with our limited manpower. We have asked the government to address it politically. We will play a bridging role.”

Around 2,000 police personnel, 10 platoons of Border Guard Bangladesh, eight platoons of Ansar Battalion and members of other forces have been deployed in Gopalganj.

Security has also been reinforced around key infrastructure, highways and urban areas, including the Padma Bridge.

In the capital, Dhaka Metropolitan Police is preparing a major operation against AL and members of affiliated organisations who allegedly fled violence-hit districts and took shelter in Dhaka.

DMP Additional Deputy Commissioner Niaz Mehedi said checkpoints and patrols had been increased. Several organisers and political figures had already been arrested, while an operation targeting those in hiding or on the run would begin soon.

Uniformed and plainclothes police have been deployed at government facilities and other key point installations, while cyber surveillance has been intensified, he added.

Detective Branch chief Mohammad Shafiqul Islam said patrol police and DB teams were conducting regular operations and had arrested suspects in connection with crude bomb explosions.

Maximum manpower had been deployed to prevent sabotage in view of the AL’s programme, he added.

Special Response Battalion Director General Faruk Ahmed said, “We are on the ground. We are working shoulder to shoulder with other law enforcement agencies. I want to assure the people that the law and order situation in the country will remain normal.”

Kamarum Munira, assistant inspector general (Media and Public Relations) at Police Headquarters, said police would take lawful action against anyone involved in violence, sabotage or obstruction of public movement in the name of a banned organisation’s programme. Police would maintain surveillance and protect lives and property while ensuring that no innocent person was harassed, she added.

Maj Gen (retd) Fazle Elahi Akbar, chairman of Foundation for Strategic and Development Studies, said attempts might be under way, possibly with external support, to destabilise the elected government. Urging the government to assess its shortcomings and adopt a clearer strategy, he said, “I would strongly recommend that the government tightens its belt and gives no more leeway for such unwanted happenings, which are destabilising both the economic and law and order situations.”

articles.title: China, Russia and US commit to safeguarding global peace, stability
articles.content:
SHENZHEN – The leaders of China, Russia and the United States stressed their shared commitment to maintaining strategic stability and international security at a historic trilateral summit on Thursday, pledging to advance United Nations reform, increase energy supplies and hold talks on reducing nuclear risks.

President Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump made the commitment in the China-Russia-US Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, issued following their unprecedented trilateral meeting in Shenzhen, Guangdong province.

“The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought,” the declaration said, adding that the three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

As permanent members of the UN Security Council, the three countries will remain committed to reforming the UN so that it can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security.

On energy security, the three countries announced plans to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products, while reaffirming the importance of maintaining stable global energy supplies.

The declaration also addressed the jurisdiction of international judicial institutions. The three leaders agreed that the International Criminal Court and other similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction.

Xi, while presiding over the summit, described the first-ever gathering of the three countries’ top leaders as “groundbreaking”. He said history has shown that peace among major countries brings stability to the world, while their contention would only lead to chaos in the world.

He stressed that humanity, living in the same global village, is “a community with a shared future where we all stand to benefit or lose together”.

In this global village, major countries shoulder special responsibilities, with their positive interaction being “not optional, but a must”, he said.

Xi called on the three countries to set good examples, work together to meet global challenges, jointly uphold world peace and stability, and make a greater contribution to the progress of humanity.

The Chinese president made a four-point proposal on how major countries could find the right way to get along and jointly underpin world peace — staying committed to mutual respect, peaceful coexistence, win-win cooperation, and dialogue and consultation.

On mutual respect, he highlighted the need for the three countries to respect one another’s sovereignty and territorial integrity, social systems and development paths of their own choice, and their respective core interests and major concerns.

On peaceful coexistence, Xi said China, Russia and the US should be partners and friends and avoid conflict or confrontation.

The Thucydides Trap is by no means a destiny, he added.

Turning to economic cooperation, Xi highlighted the complementary strengths of the three economies and urged them to expand trade and economic ties rather than pursue decoupling or disruptions to supply chains.

On dialogue and consultation, he urged joint efforts from the three countries to maintain regular high-level exchanges, keep dialogue channels open at all levels, and establish crisis communication and prevention mechanisms, to ensure that “misjudgments occur less, differences can be managed, and frictions will not escalate”.

The international community expects major countries to do more to promote peace talks, Xi pointed out, while stressing that China, Russia and the US should continue to encourage parties to a conflict to sit down and talk, and settle disputes through political and diplomatic means.

Wrapping up the gathering, Xi described the summit as “positive, constructive and fruitful”, saying the three countries share the same view on safeguarding world peace.

As long as dialogue continues and the door to engagement remains open, there is hope for peace, Xi said, while expressing confidence that the seeds planted at the Shen­zhen summit would take root and bear fruit.

Putin emphasized the importance of sovereign equality, noninterference in internal affairs and finding mutually acceptable solutions through dialogue and cooperation.

Russia stands ready to work with China and the US on the basis of mutual respect and equality, peacefully manage differences, promote free and open international trade, and strengthen cooperation on energy and food security and global governance of artificial intelligence, he said.

Trump told the two leaders that the three nuclear powers bear an important responsibility for maintaining global peace and stability, stressing the need to prevent nuclear proliferation and avoid the catastrophic consequences of nuclear weapons.

The joint declaration from the China-Russia-US summit indicated that the unprecedented gathering has been successful and has yielded significant outcomes, said Wu Xinbo, dean of the Institute of International Studies at Fudan University.

Wu said the four-point proposal put forward by Xi is crucial not only to shaping a new type of major-country relations, but also to guiding relations among countries more broadly in a changing international landscape.

He rejected comparisons between the Shenzhen summit and the 1945 Yalta Conference, arguing that the two gatherings differed fundamentally in their purposes.

The Yalta Conference was primarily concerned with the postwar division of spheres of influence among major powers, whereas the Shenzhen summit sought to strengthen cooperation among the three countries to promote global peace, security, stability, development and governance, he said.

Zhu Feng, dean of the School of International Studies at Nanjing University, said the summit and its declaration reflected a new approach to addressing the challenges of the times.

The declaration’s central message was that major countries share responsibility for safeguarding world peace, without which sustainable development cannot be achieved, Zhu said. He described the summit as a major breakthrough in head-of-state diplomacy, saying it had helped the three countries establish a greater degree of common understanding about their responsibilities in managing international affairs.

articles.title: Pakistan, Qatar reaffirm commitment to strengthening bilateral relations in security, counter-terrorism: military
articles.content:
ISLAMABAD – Pakistan and Qatar reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening bilateral relations in the areas of institutional cooperation, security and counter-terrorism on Thursday, the military’s media affairs wing said.

The development cam as Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir met with Qatar’s Interior Minister Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, who is currently visiting Pakistan, in Rawalpindi on Thursday, according to a statement by Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR).

During the meeting, they discussed matters of mutual interest and the evolving regional and global security situation. They also discussed avenues for the enhancement of bilateral security cooperation, ISPR said.

“Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to further strengthening bilateral relations between the two countries, particularly in the fields of security, counter-terrorism and institutional cooperation,” the statement said.

The visiting dignitary appreciated Pakistan’s role in promoting regional peace and stability and acknowledged the longstanding fraternal ties between the two countries, it added.

CDF Munir reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to further deepen bilateral engagement with Qatar. He underscored the importance of close cooperation in addressing shared security challenges, the statement said.

MoU signed on security cooperation

The two countries earlier signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) on security cooperation, along with an action plan to prevent drug smuggling.

The MoU was signed between Qatar’s Internal Security Force (Lekhwiya) and the Federal Constabulary, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi and Qatari counterpart Al Thani signed the documents. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also witnessed the signing ceremony, the statement said.

The PMO handout said that the premier “warmly” welcomed the visiting dignitary on “on his first visit to Pakistan and reaffirmed the longstanding brotherly relations between Pakistan and Qatar”.

“He expressed the hope that the visit would further strengthen cooperation between the ministries of interior and relevant institutions of the two brotherly countries,” it said.

PM Shehbaz also conveyed his greetings to the Qatari emir and thanked the country’s leadership for its “unwavering support to Pakistan”.

“He particularly appreciated Qatar’s continued supply of liquefied natural gas, which contributes to meeting Pakistan’s energy requirements,” the statement said.

PM Shehbaz highlighted that nearly 300,000 Pakistanis work in Qatar, where they play an important role in the country’s development and prosperity.

He said that there were extensive opportunities to expand Pakistan-Qatar economic cooperation, particularly in trade and investment, agriculture, livestock, information technology and mining and minerals.

The statement said that the Qatari minister thanked Pakistan for its hospitality. He also conveyed Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani’s congratulatory messages and best wishes to the prime minister.

“He appreciated Pakistan’s role and efforts for promoting peace and stability in the region,” the statement added.

According to a separate statement by the interior ministry, Naqvi and his counterpart also agreed to expand the scope of the exchange programme for police officers.

The two also agreed to enhance cooperation between Qatar’s National Cyber Security Agency and the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency.

“A decision was made to improve coordination between the two interior ministries to enhance bilateral cooperation,” the statement said.

It added that Qatar would also build a modern firing range at the National Police Academy. Naqvi thanked Qatar for providing the Anti-Narcotics Force with modern scanners, adding that “joint operations and information sharing” between the relevant agencies of the two countries were ongoing.

“With joint cooperation between Pakistan and Qatar, 300 drug cases have been busted over the past four years,” Naqvi was quoted as saying.

“We want to ensure that our territory is never used for drug smuggling,” the interior minister said.

“Cybercrime is an international problem, and Pakistan is taking robust measures to combat it,” he added.

Last month, in a meeting in Doha, Naqvi and the Qatari counterpart agreed to strengthen bilateral cooperation in internal security.

articles.title: How Republicans can win back MAGA and MAHA voters
articles.content:
Podcast: Play in new window | Download | Embed

Subscribe: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | iHeartRadio | Podcast Index | RSS

Republicans cannot rebuild trust by demanding loyalty from voters whose concerns they have brushed aside. The party’s election losses should force an honest reckoning with conservatives, independents, and Make America Healthy Again supporters who expected promises to become action.

Robert F. Kennedy Jr. brought together people who rarely shared a political home. Many backed Donald Trump because they believed Kennedy would have room to confront corporate influence and help families get healthier. Their support came with expectations.

The administration’s approach to glyphosate and its support for Bayer and Monsanto in litigation alienated people who considered chemical accountability central to that bargain. For voters drawn to the promise of peace, the Iran war deepened the sense that the administration had abandoned its campaign commitments.

My view is that these broken expectations help explain why Republicans lost support. Calling disappointed voters disloyal will do nothing to bring them back.

That frustration should not erase the work Kennedy has advanced. Connecting schools with local farms, encouraging scratch cooking, improving hospital meals, and pushing food companies away from artificial dyes reflect priorities worth pursuing. Kennedy is the health secretary, not the president. Entrenched interests remain formidable.

MAHA belongs to the families who want healthier children. Its future does not depend on one administration or Kennedy holding office.

Rebuilding political trust starts close to home. In Ohio, Republican organizations should stop endorsing candidates in contested primaries. Let voters examine records and choose without party machinery narrowing the field before ballots are cast.

County committees, local advocates, and independent-minded citizens can make that change. They can support farmers, scrutinize candidates, and insist that constitutional principles mean something after Election Day.

Republicans have an opportunity to listen, accept responsibility, and earn back support. That work begins with respecting voters who refuse to surrender their principles for a party label.

What happens when you’ve prayed your way through the darkest chapter of your life, only to discover that the nightmare you thought was behind you has returned?

Phil Zielke was young, healthy, and looking forward to a future filled with possibilities when cancer entered his life. Nothing could have prepared him for what followed. The physical suffering was frightening enough. The uncertainty surrounding his illness brought a different kind of fear, one that grew as he searched for answers and struggled to understand what was happening inside his own body.

As a physician, I found parts of Phil’s experience particularly troubling. There were warning signs that deserved closer attention and opportunities to investigate that were missed. His experience raises serious questions about what happens when patients place their trust in a medical system that cannot seem to explain why they are getting sicker. And when your life may depend on finding the right answers, how long can you afford to wait?

Phil eventually faced a diagnosis that would force him to confront his own mortality at an age when most people rarely consider it. His faith became deeply personal as he wrestled with circumstances beyond his control. A prayer spoken by his father would remain with him long after that moment, shaping his understanding of suffering in ways he could never have anticipated.

Then came a second confrontation with cancer.

There is something profoundly unsettling about surviving a life-threatening illness and discovering that the experience may have been only the beginning. Phil had already endured what many people fear most. He had fought to reclaim the future that cancer threatened to take from him. When that future was placed in jeopardy again, his response surprised even him.

His experience raises difficult questions about faith that people often hesitate to ask aloud. What happens when suffering returns after you’ve already endured so much? How do you reconcile anger toward God with a lifetime of believing in His goodness? And what does it actually mean to find something good in circumstances you would never have chosen?

Phil’s book, Seeing the Good in It: A Personal Story of Finding Hope in Times of Suffering, grew from experiences that challenged some of his deepest convictions. His story also raises important questions about the role of patient advocacy and the people we depend upon when our health is at stake.

There is a moment in Phil’s story when everything he believed about suffering was tested again. His experience deserves to be heard, especially by anyone who has ever wondered how much more they could possibly endure.

Meet the Guest

Phil Zielke is a speaker, teacher, coach, and two-time survivor of non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma. Diagnosed at 22 after nearly a year of unexplained illness, Phil has turned his experiences into a commitment to supporting people navigating cancer and serious illness. His book, Seeing the Good in It: A Personal Story of Finding Hope in Times of Suffering, explores his experiences with suffering through the lens of Christian faith. His work emphasizes the importance of patient advocacy and the personal challenges of confronting life-threatening illness.

Transcript Summary of this podcast episode ⤵

Cancer can strip away the illusion that we control our lives. It can interrupt a wedding, empty a classroom, and turn a trip to the mailbox into an exhausting undertaking. No one should have to face that fear alone.

Phil Zelke learned this twice. At 22, after roughly a year of weight loss, night sweats, pain, and repeated misdiagnoses, he learned he had non-Hodgkin’s lymphoma. Later, three months before his wedding, the cancer returned at stage four.

His experience carries a message patients need to hear: Keep asking questions. Seek capable care. Bring someone who can listen, help you navigate decisions, and advocate when you are too exhausted to speak.

The need for care reaches beyond treatment. Zelke endured chemotherapy and a stem cell transplant. He also needed the steady presence of his future wife, his father beside his hospital bed, and encouragement that reached him when visitors could not.

For two years, cards arrived every week. His grandfather brought a Bible with passages about hope, strength, and peace highlighted. Zelke credits his Christian faith with helping him surrender anger and find peace amid suffering.

That support became the foundation of Phil’s Friends, a ministry providing Christ-centered encouragement to people with cancer. Care packages contain practical comforts, including blankets, journals, and a Bible. Cards and prayers continue after the package arrives.

This is faith put to work. A frightened patient does not need another person trying to explain everything or force a cheerful response. Sometimes the greatest gift is simply staying close.

We do not need to wait for a diagnosis to reconsider our priorities. Make time to pray. Be present for someone who is hurting. Send the card. Offer the help.

When suffering comes, draw near to God. Take a breath, pray, and let others walk beside you through it.
