So during the second time that I had cancer, stage four cancer, it was during my stem cell transplant. So I’d done six months of chemotherapy, then they used my own my own stem cells.

So basically took an in-and-out tube in my neck. Those stem cells went into almost what looks like a dialysis dialysis machine into a bag. And then I went in for seven days of lethal chemotherapy. It was during that time where I was hooked up to tubes for feeding on oxygen.

My body was completely almost gray, and it’s where the common cold can really kill a person when you have no immunity to anything. And then they’ll put those stem cells back into you. And I remember they came in, you almost can’t see correctly. There’s so many things that are going on.

The pain is so bad, I’ve been on morphine, all these pain medications. But I remember they came in their white suits, all the nurses and people that were there and completely almost like hazmatted, hazmatted up, and came and gave me that stem cell. And I one thing my wife always says now, she goes, Oh, it the worst thing was being in that room. And it smelled like cream corn, and she hates cream corn to this day because of the way that that smelled.

So it must have been some some of the concoction that was, a part of it. But it was during those times where I thought it was gonna be my time to leave this earth. And that’s when I hit my breaking point. And I cried out to God and I said, Lord, if it’s time for me to go to heaven, I’m ready.

I believe Jesus died for me. I don’t want to be in this pain. But if not, if it’s not my time, you can have the rest of my life. You can use me however you want.

And so through that, I really made a promise to God on my hostel bed, realizing that the only reason I’m gonna live to see tomorrow is if God, if it’s in God’s plan for me to see tomorrow, here on earth. And so I started getting a little better and I started setting these little bite-sized goals. And so one day I wanted to sit on the edge of the bed by myself, eventually make it out in the hallway. So I’d have my IV pole with me and a nurse or family member by my side.

And that first day, which I think it’s important for all of us, whether we’re going through a sickness or not, to have these little bite-sized goals because we were really feel good about our accomplishments. And so I set my sights on that very first door. And so I made it to the first door, eventually back to my room the next day to the second door. Eventually I’d make it all the way around the hospital hallway.

Well, I was the old guy at 22 and 23, treated in pediatrics. So there were two-year-olds and 10-year-olds and young fathers. And and every time I stopped at that door, I saw kids and I saw young adults who had nobody. And I thought, this is the hardest thing I’ve ever had to go through.

And people are walking this journey all alone. And if you think about it, the mortgage still has to be paid. There’s other siblings involved, there’s already broken families all over. And now someone has cancer and the stress that it causes on people.

And so knowing that there’s so many people and going through cancer, I wrote in that journal of all the things that people did for me. And so it was about a week after I was diagnosed, a group of people put a care package together for me. They all signed their names to it. They said they’re thinking about me and praying for me.

That act of kindness caused me to break down and cry for a few reasons. Number one, to know that it was okay to accept other people’s help. Number two, there were people who took time out of their busy schedules to do this for me that I didn’t even know. And third, I was going to learn about the power of prayer as I, journeyed through my disease.

And then when I was well enough to be at home, I’d lay upstairs on the couch and I’d look forward to when it was one o’clock. So I’d wear a watch. And why one o’clock? Because that’s when the mailman came.

And so I’d work my energy the edge of the couch, down the stairs, out to the front door, and mailboxes on the front porch. So I’d put my hand in there and I’d pull mail out. Well, every week for two years, I pulled a card out with my name on it. And so even if that journey from upstairs to downstairs could wear me out for that day, once I had that card of encouragement in my hand, it gave me the strength to go back up the stairs again.

And so I’d sit down, and a lot of times it’d be hard to open, open the envelope just because of all the side effects from the treatments. And but every time that card came exactly at the right time with exactly the right message. If I was weak, it could be a verse such as Philippians 4, 13. I could do all things through Christ who gives me strength.

And so I could hold on to that verse now for the entire next day, which would get me through those moments. And then I had my grandfather who traveled 300 miles and he he woke up one, I woke up one day in my hospital room. He was sitting in the corner of my room. There were, you’re talking about how many, Dr. T, how many books that you read.

That’s the exact same person my grandfather was. And he was a lifelong learner. And so he had papers all over the place. But what he said is, Phil, I went to your house and I grabbed your Bible, which is on your shelf.

And obviously, we know if a Bible just sits on a shelf, it’s no good to us. It’s like any other book that that hasn’t been read. And obviously God’s word is powerful and true. And so he highlighted all the verses with hope and strength and peace.

And then he walked over to my bedside, he looked me in the eyes and he said, Phil, I need to tell you something. Your Graham and I, we love you. But most importantly, your Heavenly Father does. He took the Bible, put it on my nightstand, and he walked out.

So when I couldn’t have visitors or didn’t want visitors, God’s word is that went on and on in my head and in my heart is where I got my hope and my strength from. And so in my journal, the pages and many tears, in my journal, that’s when the whole prompting for Phil’s friends began. It was seeing a great need. And this year, 2.2 million Americans will hear the words that they have cancer for the very first time.

1,500 or more Americans lose their lives every single day. And so it’s urgent that we get out and we provide hope to people, let people know they’re not alone, tell people about Jesus, let them know that they have a God that loves them and wants to walk this journey with them, someone they can pray to, someone that can walk, take them by the hand as they’re walking through the fire, so to say. And so I looked at the care package, the cards, and the prayers and the visits. And so that’s how we launched Phil’s Friends with the mission of providing Christ-centered support and hope to people going through cancer.

So if anybody with cancer anywhere across the country, go to our website, philzfriends.org, which is p-h-il s friends.org. Request a care package for anyone of any age, any type of cancer, anywhere across the country. And you put in their information as the patient and then yours as the requester. And then we have hope centers.

So we have four bricks and mortar locations. By the end of next year, we’ll have six. And so people can come in in there and pack care packages, make cards, volunteer for 90 minutes. And then every time a care package is packed, we have a first name and an age and state, and we ring a bell because we always say bringing hope is fun.

And so we’re able to ring the bell and celebrate. And this other care package shows up. And then after that, we’ll send cards of hope the same way I got cards, and we’ll pray for people. And so that’s what we do at Phil’s Friends.

We started with one person, and now we’re gonna now we’re helping about 80,000 patients and family since we began. Wow, that’s amazing. What are the some of the things that are in the care package? Yeah, so let me show you.

So the care package goes out in a box, and it’s not like the normal Amazon box that just shows up on, well, a lot show up on my doorstep. They have my name on it, but I don’t I don’t order them. And so one thing that’s on here, you can see there’s different artwork that goes inside. So it has the word hope.

There’s also Phil’s friends logo on there, and then inside the care package, we have certain items. We have drawstring bags for men and for women. So women go out in green bags, men go out in in blue bags, and then kids are based on gender and and age. But one thing we have in each package is a blanket.

And so obviously inside the hospital or at home, and people can have collections for a lot of these items, and that’s how we we get those and fulfill our needs. So there’s a fleece tied blanket that goes inside of there or other blankets. If it’s a kids’ care package, they’ll have teddy bears that go in there. We have a journal, just as I kept a journal.

And so these are typically done by people who love scrapbooking, and they can get these done on their journals, and then there’s a matching card that goes inside of it. There’s word search puzzles and seducco books because there’s a lot of time to pass. This one is a port pillow, so I’ve had a port a few different times, but has velcro on it, and that can get Velcro on the seat belt, and then if you have to stop quickly, it’ll help with the pain. There’s hats that are handmade and store-bought, fuzzy socks for women, there’s Kleenex and playing cards to pass time.

There’s lotion and chapsticks. So a lot of items that go in there, but the most important item that we put in is the Bible because we want to make sure that we can get God’s word out to everybody. So the fact that we’re sending our 80,000th care package now means that there’s 80,000 Bibles that have gone out, 80,000 blankets. And we just want to make sure we can get God’s word in in front of people’s hands.

And so that’s what we really feel called to do is to comfort people and provide support that way. And then the first thing that people see when they open a care package is a card. And on that card says, someone is anonymously requested a Phil’s friends care package, especially for you. And then there’s a lot of names that go on on this.

So it’s all the names of the people that personalized and made this care package for them. So when they open it on their doorstep, they’ll realize, wow, this is first of all, this box is incredible. It’s artfully decorated. If we know certain likes that they have, our volunteers and artists on the outside of the boxes will draw that.

And so they’ll get the care package, they’ll know who it’s from, they’ll feel comforted and loved. And then after that, the cards of hope will continue. And we have kids as young as three years old that’ll make these cards, and adults, as as old as a hundred or a hundred and three, I think, that have made cards. And so we hear back all the time how meaningful those cards are.

People put them on the refrigerator, they’ll put them on their post them on their walls, or put them in scrapbooks if you just need a place to cry. And when I was going through my journey, I had a place in my basement where I put all the cards and everything up. And if it was just I needed to go down and be encouraged or have a good cry, that’s that’s where I would go. And so that’s that’s our care packages.

And our vision for this as we move forward is to support as many people as we can in this way, getting the care package and the cards and the visits and the prayer. And so another way that we can do that is through our hospital program. So we have hospitals that will jump on and nurses inside those hospitals that are Christian, that we will train them up, we’ll get them the care package, and then they can deliver that to the patients that are there. Yep.

And then we also have a partnership guide. All this is available online at philzriends.org, but it’s basically all the different ways that people can get involved through volunteering, how to request a care package, and it talks a little bit about our vision, which is in the next three years, we want to be able to double the people that we’re supporting. So right now it’s 12,000. By the end of 2029, we want to have that at 25,000 patients and families.

We had 80,000 volunteer hours last year, want to get to 160,000. And then we’re gonna open two new facilities next year. We’re gonna expand from the Chicagoland area down into the Orlando area. And so that’ll be our next regional hub down there because right now we’re supporting over 2,000 patients just in the state of Florida without a facility.

Wow, what that is just amazing. It’s just the whole time you were talking, I was just having goosebumps because it was just such a cool thing. Now, do you have sponsorships? Is that how you end up with Bibles to give away and books and notebooks and all sorts of things?

Yeah, so we have an approved care package item list that people go to our website, philzfriends.org, and and then those can go through Amazon or they can get shipped to our facilities. Then we have people that’ll sign up to sponsor, a monthly donor, which they can do. It costs us $100 to get a care package out and another $25 to send cards for a year. So it’s $125 to support a patient for a year.

And then we have companies and churches and schools and organizations, civic organizations that’ll volunteer with us. And then we also will go to them and have packing events. We’ve done them in Orange County, California. We’ve done them down in Florida, a lot of places throughout the United States.

And then we have what’s called satellite locations where we can, if God is calling a person, we can train them up, give them the resources and the tools to support people in their local area. So when we started, we had zero in the bank. Every year it’s our goal to raise more and more funding so that we can support more people. And we’ve never turned anybody away for a care package, even with this need.

So God’s had his hand on this the entire time. And the fact that I’m here after having stage four cancer twice, so many people’s lives that are being touched by so many other people through Phil’s friends, it’s a testament to how good God is and how great his plans are for this ministry and just wanting people, if we look at one verse about love, Jesus says, love the Lord your God with all your heart, all your mind, all your soul, and all your strength, and love your neighbor as yourself and to visit the sick. So that’s what we’re doing. It’s his command, and that’s why he’s blessing it.

So it’s not about us going out and saying, Oh, we gotta gather all these resources before we go. No, God says take a step of faith, take a step or a step of faith, messing up on my words here, take a step of faith and go. And then I’ll I will provide what’s needed. And so I think that’s the test of faith for all of us as God calls us to do something, go do it and let Him take care of the needs.

Let Him figure out how it’s gonna work. Is this your full-time vocation now? It is. So I taught off and on from 2004 to 2009, launched it out of my basement, and I’ve been full-time since 2009.

Yeah. And how many people work in your organization? I know you mentioned a lot of volunteers, but do you have actual structured paid people in your organization? Yes.

So we have an operations person. There’s only two of us full-time, myself and the operations person, and then we have a handful of part-timers that will help in our hope centers or with our hospital program, doing some outreach. So we we stay very minimal when it comes to administrative costs. 92% of every donation that comes in goes directly out the door.

Oh man, that is just amazing. Just absolutely amazing. And you do you ship internationally also? We don’t ship internationally, but what we will do is say if you knew somebody in a different country, we could get the care package to you, and then you guys could take care of the shipping.

But we’ve also done things in like Liberia and other places where we’ve connected with missionaries. So we’ll get them the care packages. They go over, then they send us they send us videos and testimonials of all the great work that’s being done. That is just amazing, just absolutely amazing.

And and one more time, I just want to make sure that because you went through that quick. One more time. Where what can where can people find out and show that box again? Because that box is really super cool.

Super cool. Could you imagine if you were it doesn’t matter if you’re a child or if you’re an adult and you get a box like that in your that comes to your front door, it would just I think it would make you a combination, it would make you smile and make you cry at the same time that something like that’s gonna come. And so many of those things that you had in your that you showed in the care package is like a little bit unisex and also age ageless from from kids all the way to adults. Yeah, exactly.

And the reason that came to be is I kept a journal the whole, for those couple of years I was sick and what was important. And so that’s how a lot of these items came to be. And people can actually print off a list and then pick things that they want to donate to a particular center. They can do that.

Yeah, at Phil’sfriends.org. They can get an approved care package item list, they can find partnership guides. There’s encouraging videos that are on there. We also have cards of hope.

Those are printable templates, so they have a joke on them as well as a prayer. You write your first name and your age. We always tell people don’t lie about your age. And the reason is, I mean, obviously we’re not supposed to lie, but secondly, it’s important to get it.

We hear all back all the time from the patients we support. Well, I got a card from a five-year-old this time. Now I got one from someone who’s 80. I got, one from someone in Texas, and now I got someone, a card from someone in Iowa.

And so it’s great to have the, to know that so many people are in your corner as you’re going through this disease. That’s really great. And I love the fact that you send a Bible out. Are are there other Christian-based things that are in your boxes that can encourage people to get into the Bible and get into like even a Bible app or something like that?

Because it’s one thing, like you just mentioned, about having a book that never gets read. Well, if you have a Bible that never gets read, it doesn’t do its job. How do you encourage people to dig into that? Yeah, it doesn’t.

We have a letter as well that goes in there. It’s my personal story just on one page and explains the gospel because there’s a lot of people that’ll get this and they’ll get news that’s heartbreaking and say, I only have a month to live, or whatever that looks like. We want to make sure that people are understanding the gospel. Well, and that’s another thing about cancer that has always bugged me.

I mean, the only people that the only person that knows how long you’re gonna live is God. That’s right. He numbered the day, the the hairs on your head and then knows the number of breaths and the number of heartbeats you’re gonna have. And it’s always bothered me when oncologists come in and say, Well, you’ve got four months to live.

I agree. Because it just smacks people in a way. I I’ve done an interview with with a gentleman that wrote a book about terminal cancer as a misdiagnosis, and he uses new German medicine to to diagnose and to unwind that with people. And I remember first learning about new medicine many, many years ago that they say that when you’ve had an emotional, really an emotional hit, which like you have four years, four months to live, is an emotional hit.

It actually is a visible thing that can you you can see on a brain CAT scan. It looks like a bullseye, you can actually see it. And and how radiologists interpret it, they they call it an artifact that, but it really is an emotional hurt, it hit. And this doctor, Dr. Hammer, was is able to use CAT scans for 50 years.

He saw 50,000 patients and was able to show that so much of what happened to them was an emotional hit. And I think that oncologists just take the hammer and hammer it home even more. Like, and so I always tell people when you get a cancer diagnosis, the first thing you need to do, the very first thing you need to do is sit down and take a deep breath. Just sit down and take a deep breath.

This didn’t happen, it’s it’s not a five alarm fire. It’s not like you’re breathing to death or you’re choking and you can’t breathe. I mean, there are things that that are five alarm fires in medicine. I’m a was a board certified emergency physician, so I know what five what five alarm fires look like, and cancer ain’t one of them.

It’s taken a while to get there. So sit, sit down, take a deep breath, look at your options, and pray that God helps you to lead to the right people from the beginning. That’s exactly right. And I know in God’s word it says none of us even know about tomorrow.

Today is enough to worry about itself. So we’re not thinking when we don’t have a diagnosis, oh what we’re gonna live a little differently when we hear those things, which is good, and that could help us some perspective, but you’re right. Sit down, take a deep breath, and pray. Yeah, because it’s it’s not an emergency, it’s an urgency.

You need to do something about it, but it’s not an emergency that if you don’t do something about it in the next five minutes, you’re gonna die. Right. And oncology would tend to lead you to believe that, that now you that they finally got a diagnosis. We have to hurry up.

I’ve had patients over the years that had a had a mammogram on Monday, a biopsy on Tuesday, and on Wednesday they were, in the talking to the oncologist, and on Friday they got started on their chemotherapy when they didn’t even have a minute to process it and decide what was going on. So I think that get encouraging people to open that Bible and start reading it, start doing research is just such a blessing, Phil. I mean, what you’re doing with this organization is just really super amazing. Well, thank you.

It’s part of God’s plan, and we have so many amazing people that are a part of it. And I’m just one and we have thousands, that are involved, which is that’s the really cool thing to see because God’s the one who gave the vision. Obviously, there’s a lot of hard work and pressing forward, but it’s the way he uses so many people and calls so many people to help others. And and just to close the loop a little bit, when you talked about in the beginning about perspective, just getting into God’s word, that is where the perspective comes from.

If we don’t have his perspective, we literally are have no perspective. It’s just like the world and it’s it’s failing, it’s falling away. So thanks for thanks for your wisdom on that. Well, we’ve got about two minutes left.

What would you like to say in closing to our audience today as we’re as we’re ending our time here together? So, first of all, Dr. T, thanks for allowing me to be on today and share the story. It’s a privilege to be able to write the book, seeing the good in it. And when we think about seeing the good in it, it’s really seeing God in it.

We want people to be able to see God in your circumstance, whether it’s yours or your family’s or any type of hardship, because God is there. So don’t turn your back on him. I’d encourage you, as in James 4.8 again, to draw near to God. He’ll draw near to you.

And then secondly, if you have somebody that is going through cancer, I would encourage you today to go to phil’sfriends.org. So Phil’s Friends, P-H-I-L-S, F-R-I-E-N-D-S dot or G. Request a care package. This next week it’ll get sent and show up anonymously on your friend or your family member’s doorstep, anywhere across the country. It’s for any age.

And also if you want to get involved and put your faith into action, it’s another reason that we exist at Phil’s Friends is to help empower you, whether it’s getting a care package and taking it to someone, working on our cards of hope that you can do in a variety of settings, or get involved, through giving those ways. But thank you so much for allowing me to be on here. And just in closing, too, just to remember, to take a deep breath, sit down and pray. And pray.

Well, Phil, thank you so much for your book. Thank you so much for your time. And this is a great conversation, and I’m sure it’s going to be very enlightening and upbeating, and particularly Phil’s friends to a lot of other people. So I want to thank you for being here today.

Thank you for all of the people who’ve joined us here today or in the future. And we’ll close out with one of my favorite verses from the Bible I close all of my podcasts with, whether they are live or pre-recorded, which is Romans 12, 12. Rejoice in hope, be patient in trouble, and be persistent in prayer. Remember to lean into God, trust him for everything.

He’ll never let you down. His timeline may not be your timeline, but he promised to be with you every step of the way. So we’ll see you here tomorrow or the next time on The Tenpenny Files. Have a great rest of your day, everybody.

Goodbye and God bless. You.

articles.title: Deepfake Elon Musk  nearly costs viewers $4.7 million in crypto
articles.content:
.kadence-column491016_350891-b2 > .kadence-column491016_350891-b2 > .kadence-column491016_350891-b2 > .kadence-column491016_350891-b2 > .kt-inside-inner-col > .kadence-column491016_350891-b2 > .kadence-column491016_350891-b2 > .kt-inside-inner-col:before{opacity:0.3;}@media all and (max-width: 1024px){.kadence-column491016_350891-b2 > }@media all and (max-width: 767px){.kadence-column491016_350891-b2 > }

In this article

  • A fake Tesla livestream used an Elon Musk deepfake to push a crypto scam
  • Coinbase says it blocked $4.7 million in attempted transfers
  • A giveaway that asks you to send crypto first to get more back is a scam

Coinbase says it stopped about $4.7 million in attempted payments to a fake cryptocurrency giveaway. The scam didn’t rely on breaking into customers’ accounts. It persuaded them to send money themselves.

Imagine you’re watching a Tesla event on YouTube when Elon Musk appears with an unexpected offer: send cryptocurrency to the address shown, and you’ll get twice as much back. A QR code makes it easy to pay, while the livestream pressures you to act before the offer disappears. You open your crypto app, enter the payment details, and prepare to confirm.

According to Coinbase, that is exactly what happened when a fake Elon Musk livestream prompted hundreds of its customers to attempt payments to scammers. The customers were logged in and approving the payments themselves. That made the transfers look authorized, even though the customers had been tricked into sending money. Coinbase describes this as a central challenge in detecting the scam.

Reportedly, Coinbase’s automated scam defenses prevented roughly $4.7 million—about 91% of the money involved in those attempted payments—from leaving customers’ accounts. That is money the company says it prevented from being sent, not money recovered after it was stolen. Coinbase hasn’t said how much ultimately reached the scammers.

Using Elon Musk’s image for this type of scam is not new. Deepfakes can make these scams more convincing. A deepfake is an image, video, or audio recording created or altered with AI to make it seem like someone said or did something they didn’t.

Scammers may need only a photo or a shockingly short clip of the real person to create a convincing deepfake. That’s not hard to find when you want to impersonate a public figure like Elon Musk.

How to stay safe

The best advice in cases like this is the usual one: if it sounds too good to be true, it probably is.

To avoid a fake cryptocurrency giveaway, you don’t need to decide whether every movement or syllable in a video is AI-generated. The payment request itself should be a clear warning.

  • Don’t send cryptocurrency to “unlock” a larger cryptocurrency payout. Promises to multiply the amount you send are a red flag.
  • Don’t treat an on-screen wallet address or QR code as proof that an offer is legitimate. Coinbase warns against sending funds to addresses displayed in videos, livestreams, or messages.
  • Close the offer and go to the company’s official website or account yourself, rather than using links supplied by the promotion.
  • Take payment warnings seriously. Pause, read the explanation, and discuss the offer with someone you trust. Or ask Malwarebytes Scam Guard if no trusted person is around.

If you already sent cryptocurrency

Cryptocurrency payments typically can’t be reversed, so there’s no guarantee of recovery. But don’t blame yourself or feel stupid; act quickly to limit further losses:

Preserve the evidence. Keep transaction records, receipts, screenshots, messages, and details of the livestream or website. Contact the exchange or service you used immediately and report the scam. In the US, you can report it to the FTC through ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

Stop communicating with the scammers. Don’t let further messages persuade you to make another payment. It is not uncommon for fake giveaways to demand additional payments to supposedly process the first transfer.

Watch out for recovery scams. That FBI agent sending you a DM is just as fake as the Elon Musk in the deepfake video.

For more advice about what to do when you’ve been scammed online, read our blog Been scammed online? Here’s what to do.

articles.title: “Christian Disagreement With Feminism Has Become Hatred of Women”
articles.content:
LTRP Note: The following is posted for informational and research purposes.

By Brandon Showalter
The Christian Post

“Feminism is cancer.” Across much of the Right-wing alt media, the podcast scene, and social media, this quip and others like it draw countless likes, reposts, and views, including from professing Christians.

Although I understand some of their objections, much of what passes for a critique of feminism online has morphed into something else: a ferocious, boiling contempt for women as a whole. I’ll be up front about how I think here. . . . As a socially conservative Evangelical, I can’t in good conscience accept many feminists’ anthropological and metaphysical claims about human nature or who God is. While abusive men in power do indeed create all kinds of problems, I disagree with the way some feminists tend to blame all the world’s ills on “the patriarchy.” Click here to read this entire article.

.kadence-column491003_6bab7a-f6 > .kadence-column491003_6bab7a-f6 > .kadence-column491003_6bab7a-f6 > .kadence-column491003_6bab7a-f6 > .kt-inside-inner-col > .kadence-column491003_6bab7a-f6 > .kadence-column491003_6bab7a-f6 > .kt-inside-inner-col:before{opacity:0.3;}@media all and (max-width: 1024px){.kadence-column491003_6bab7a-f6 > }@media all and (max-width: 767px){.kadence-column491003_6bab7a-f6 > }

In this article

  • Chrome 158 fixes 204 security issues, including six rated critical
  • Anthropic researcher Xinyang Ge used AI to find two critical flaws
  • Update Chrome to get the security fixes, including on Android

On November 17, Google issued a security update to Chrome’s Stable channel for Windows, Mac, and Linux. The update is rolling out over the coming days and weeks.

Most users are on Chrome’s Stable channel. The desktop update brings Chrome to versions 158.0.8127.36/.37 for Windows and Mac, and 158.0.8127.36 for Linux. It includes 204 security fixes, six of which are rated critical—the highest severity level.

Google also released Chrome 158.0.8127.42 for Android on November 17, with the same security fixes. It’s rolling out through Google Play. On November 18, Google released Chrome 159.0.8154.18 for Android to a small percentage of users. It will become available to more users over the next few days.

Google credits Anthropic researcher Xinyang Ge, assisted by Claude, with finding the critical GPU and Media flaws. Ge is also credited with finding several high-severity flaws.

How to update Chrome

The easiest option is to allow Chrome to update automatically. But you can fall behind on updates if you never close your browser or if something goes wrong, such as an extension preventing the update.

If you don’t want to wait for the rollout to reach you, you can update manually.

Open About Google Chrome from Chrome’s Settings or Help menu. Chrome will check for updates and download any available update. If prompted, click Relaunch to apply it.

You can find an explanation of the version numbering system and step-by-step instructions in our guide: How to update Chrome on every operating system.

Technical details

The update addresses six vulnerabilities Google rates critical, all involving memory-safety errors. These include out-of-bounds writes in GPU and ANGLE, a buffer overflow in Media, and use-after-free vulnerabilities in WebView, GarbageCollection, and WebAudio.

Graphics-related fixes also feature prominently among the high-severity entries, including additional ANGLE and GPU vulnerabilities.

I want to have a closer look at the vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-131031: a critical out-of-bounds write in GPU.

Google Chrome uses your GPU for graphics rendering, video playback, and web graphics Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) like WebGL and WebGPU.

An out-of-bounds write vulnerability allows a program to write outside the memory boundaries it is supposed to use. It can lead to memory corruption or allow an attacker to place malicious code in memory and trick the system into running it.

articles.title: Scattered Spider’s phishing and SIM-swap tactics led to six-year sentence
articles.content:
.kadence-column490927_e74642-57 > .kadence-column490927_e74642-57 > .kadence-column490927_e74642-57 > .kadence-column490927_e74642-57 > .kt-inside-inner-col > .kadence-column490927_e74642-57 > .kadence-column490927_e74642-57 > .kt-inside-inner-col:before{opacity:0.3;}@media all and (max-width: 1024px){.kadence-column490927_e74642-57 > }@media all and (max-width: 767px){.kadence-column490927_e74642-57 > }

In this article

  • Scattered Spider used phishing texts and SIM swaps to steal $11.6 million in cryptocurrency
  • Tyler Robert Buchanan’s six-year sentence doesn’t mean the wider group has disappeared
  • Follow our advice to protect your phone number and accounts from SIM swapping

A US court has sentenced a member of the Scattered Spider cybercrime group to six years in prison. Tyler Robert Buchanan, a 24-year-old British man, joins four other group members in jail for his part in crimes that netted $11.6 million in proceeds.

Texts, SIM swaps and $11.6 million

Buchanan and his co-conspirators hacked at least a dozen companies in a years-long campaign, according to the Department of Justice. They sent hundreds of SMS phishing messages, also known as smishing, to employees at their target companies. The messages pretended to come from the employer or one of its contractors, such as an IT support provider. They contained links to phishing websites impersonating company websites and designed to steal usernames and passwords. The criminal group used those stolen credentials to access company systems.

The group also used SIM swapping to steal from individuals. In a SIM swap, a criminal tricks a mobile phone carrier into transferring a victim’s phone number to a SIM card the criminal controls. The criminal can then receive calls and text messages intended for the victim, including SMS authentication codes.

SIM swapping allowed Buchanan and his co-conspirators to take over cryptocurrency accounts and wallets, stealing over $11.6 million from victims.

Buchanan was arrested in Spain in May 2024 and taken into US custody in April 2025. He pleaded guilty to one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and one count of aggravated identity theft. He faced a maximum possible sentence of 22 years.

The other four defendants in the US case have also been sentenced. The longest sentence, 10 years, went to 22-year-old Floridian Noah Michael Urban, who pleaded guilty to fraud-related charges.

Joel Martin Evans , aged 27, of North Carolina, is now serving a two-year federal prison sentence for conspiracy to commit wire fraud. Ahmed Hossam Eldin Elbadawy and Evans Onyeaka Osiebo, both from Texas, each received 45-month sentences for wire fraud and aggravated identity theft.

Does this end the reign of Scattered Spider?

Experts say it’s unlikely, partly because the group is fragmented. Cybersecurity company Group-IB has warned that it contains different subclusters connected by shared tools and techniques. Members sometimes share online chats, too, but the subclusters act separately and rarely include more than five people, the company said.

There is also a significant overlap between Scattered Spider and an online group known as The Com, Group-IB said. The Com has been linked to child sexual abuse material and attacks on companies, including Allianz Life.

Other Scattered Spider members were also sentenced in the UK in July this year. Eighteen-year-old Owen Flowers and 19-year-old Thalha Jubair each received five-and-a-half-year sentences for a cyberattack on Transport for London (TfL). The youths live-streamed that attack in August 2024, which stole the personal data of up to 10 million TfL customers.

We also reported last month on the arrest of another person linked to Scattered LAPSUS$ Hunters. The name brings together three groups—Scattered Spider, LAPSUS$, and ShinyHunters—that have reportedly worked together on and off since summer 2025.

How to protect your number from SIM swapping

Phishing texts and SIM swaps can put both work systems and personal accounts at risk. These steps can make it harder for someone to take over your number or use it to access your accounts:

  • Ask your mobile carrier whether it offers an account PIN, port-out lock, or number-transfer protection. These can make it harder for someone to move your number to another SIM.
  • Where possible, use an authenticator app, passkey, or security key instead of SMS codes. These options aren’t tied to your phone number in the same way.
  • Never approve a sign-in prompt you didn’t initiate. Attackers may flood you with requests in the hope that you’ll approve one.

Scammers know more about you than you think.

articles.title: British Prosecutors End Case Against Pastor Arrested After Criticizing Islam
articles.content:
by Stefan J. Bos, Worthy News Europe Bureau Chief

LONDON (Worthy News) – British prosecutors have decided to take no further action against a Christian pastor who was handcuffed and taken into custody in April after criticizing Islam while preaching the Gospel and singing hymns in the English town of Watford.

Steve Maile, a grandfather and senior pastor of Oasis City Church in Watford, northwest of London, was arrested on April 18 on suspicion of a racially or religiously aggravated public order offense. He was released on bail while police investigated.

According to the Christian Legal Centre, which is supporting Maile, the public order investigation concerned remarks he allegedly made about Islam and LGBTQ+ issues. The Crown Prosecution Service has since decided to take no further action.

“I am relieved that the police have finally confirmed what I knew from the beginning: I had committed no crime,” Maile said after the center announced the decision nearly seven months after his arrest.

PASTOR RECOUNTS ARREST

Maile recalled singing hymns, calling on people to repent and questioning whether Islam was a religion of peace. He wanted Muslims to come to faith in Jesus, he explained.

Footage obtained by Worthy News shows Maile continuing to preach as officers handcuffed him. “You repent and believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and you’ll be saved,” he told those nearby. The footage was widely shared on social media.

Hertfordshire Constabulary said officers had also received an assault complaint. According to the Christian Legal Centre, it involved a teenager. Maile strongly denied the allegation, and police took no further action on it while the public order investigation continued.

Maile described spending about 12 hours in custody and suffering hand injuries from the handcuffs that required medical treatment and splints. He said he called out in Jesus’ name for officers to remove the cuffs. An officer replied, “In the name of Jesus, get in the car!”

MAILE CONSIDERS CIVIL ACTION

Maile said he forgives the officers and described being handcuffed in front of his family as humiliating. He recalled sleepless nights and months of uncertainty for his family over whether he would be prosecuted. Police acknowledged his concerns and declined to comment on the specific allegations, citing possible formal complaints or legal action.

In April, Maile told supporters he intended to follow the example of the Apostle Paul, who invoked his rights as a Roman citizen. “I’ve got rights too,” Maile said, recalling Paul’s defense. “That’s what I’m going to do.”

Andrea Williams of the Christian Legal Centre pledged to continue supporting Maile as he considers civil proceedings. The Public Order Act’s provisions on stirring up religious hatred expressly protect discussion and criticism of religions and efforts to persuade people to change their beliefs.

Maile intends to continue preaching publicly, including in Watford. “I have preached for 45 years because I love people and want them to know Jesus,” he said. “I do not attack individuals, and I do not call for hatred or violence. I plead with people to come to Christ.”

FREE SPEECH DEBATE IN BRITAIN

Maile’s case comes amid a broader debate over freedom of speech and religion in Britain. Some Christians, including Maile, have expressed concern about what they see as the growing influence of Islam in British public life. The Christian Legal Centre has argued that police should protect the right to criticize any religion.

In Swindon, prosecutors dropped a public order case against Christian street preacher John Dunn in 2022 over remarks about homosexuality that he made to two women.

In Leeds, a court in 2023 overturned the conviction of street preacher David McConnell, who had been found guilty of intentionally causing harassment, alarm or distress after repeatedly referring to a transgender woman as a man.

Free speech advocates have also raised concerns about how Britain polices speech on social media, where some people convicted over their posts have received prison sentences.

The post British Prosecutors End Case Against Pastor Arrested After Criticizing Islam appeared first on Worthy Christian News.

articles.title: Churches And Lawmakers Mark Red Wednesday For Persecuted Christians
articles.content:
by Stefan J. Bos, Worthy News Europe Bureau Chief

BUDAPEST (Worthy News) – Churches, civic groups, and lawmakers in several countries have begun marking Red Wednesday by lighting landmarks in red, holding prayer vigils, and sharing testimonies to draw attention to the persecution and discrimination facing hundreds of millions of Christians worldwide.

In numerous nations, Christians risk imprisonment or death for their faith, according to researchers who monitor religious persecution. Christian advocacy group Open Doors estimates in its 2026 World Watch List that more than 388 million Christians worldwide face high levels of persecution or discrimination because of their faith.

The November 18 observance is part of Red Week, organized by the international Catholic charity Aid to the Church in Need (ACN). At least 130 cathedrals are expected to take part, along with churches and public landmarks from Australia and the Philippines to Europe and the Americas.

“They often feel alone. They feel isolated, and they need hope,” ACN International Executive President Regina Lynch said in a video message urging people to pray for persecuted Christians. She said the red lighting symbolizes the blood of martyrs.

Among those drawing attention to the plight of persecuted Christians is former Hungarian state secretary Tristan Azbej, who is scheduled to help open a Red Wednesday conference in Budapest.

RED WEDNESDAY IN BUDAPEST

Azbej leads the Axioma Center for Persecuted Christians, which is organizing the event. The gathering in Hungary’s capital will bring together church leaders, survivors, and aid workers to discuss how to protect threatened communities and get aid to them.

Roman Catholic Bishop Mark Maigida Nzukwein of Wukari is due to speak about violence against Christian communities in Nigeria. Bishop Azad Marshall of the Church of Pakistan will address the struggle for religious freedom in his country.

Axioma also lists Kandeel Adel Khaleel Alhalasa, whom it identifies as an attack survivor from Jordan.

Separately, Jordan’s State Security Court on Sunday sentenced three men to death for the October 23 shooting at a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hamoud. Nine people were killed when gunmen opened fire during a funeral.

Azbej previously coordinated government aid to persecuted Christians under then-Prime Minister Viktor Orbán.

HUNGARY HELPS PROGRAM

Hungary created a dedicated office for that work in 2016 and elevated it to a full state secretariat in 2018. Hungarian officials described the initiative as the first of its kind in the world.

The secretariat also oversaw Hungary Helps, a broader humanitarian program that Azbej said reached more than 60 countries.

“I am confident that the new government will recognize the importance of our cause as a national mission and will continue with the Hungary Helps Program,” Azbej wrote in a farewell message reviewed by Worthy News in May. He took charge of the newly launched Axioma center in September.

Budapest first joined the campaign in 2019, when the Chain Bridge over the Danube and the statue of St. Gellért were lit red. The Elisabeth Bridge was among the landmarks listed for the following year’s observance.

Sándor Palace, the Hungarian president’s official residence, and the Corinthia Hotel were among the buildings illuminated in 2025.

EUROPEAN LANDMARKS TURN RED

Paris landmarks due to be lit red this year include Notre-Dame Cathedral, the Sacré-Cœur Basilica, the Pont Neuf bridge, and the obelisk on the Place de la Concorde.

More than 250 sites are expected to take part in Spain, including Madrid’s Almudena Cathedral and Neptune Fountain and the Aljafería Palace in Zaragoza, which houses Aragon’s regional parliament.

A cross-party group at the European Parliament will hold a conference in Brussels on Wednesday on how the European Union can defend freedom of religion or belief. The parliament’s building in Strasbourg is scheduled to be lit red on November 23.

Croatia’s parliament building in Zagreb is also expected to be illuminated, and young Christians from Syria and Pakistan are due to speak at a conference there on Friday.

St. George’s Cathedral in Southwark, London, will host a Mass marking 10 years since Britain’s first Red Wednesday. ACN plans to honor Sister Annie Demerjian, who stayed in Aleppo during Syria’s civil war to help families and other vulnerable residents.

The post Churches And Lawmakers Mark Red Wednesday For Persecuted Christians appeared first on Worthy Christian News.

articles.title: Nearly 5,000 Christians Killed Worldwide as New Reports Expose Massacres, Burned Churches and Forced Child Marriages
articles.content:
by Emmitt Barry, Worthy News Washington D.C. Bureau Chief

(Worthy News) – Nearly 5,000 Christians were killed for their faith worldwide during a recent 12-month period, with Nigeria accounting for more than 70 percent of the deaths, according to new findings from Christian persecution watchdogs documenting massacres, church attacks, kidnappings, forced conversions and the sexual exploitation of Christian women and girls.

The 2026 World Watch List, published by Open Doors, recorded 4,849 Christians killed for faith-related reasons between October 2024 and September 2025, including 3,490 in Nigeria alone. The organization estimates that more than 388 million Christians worldwide—approximately one in seven believers—face high levels of persecution or discrimination.

Sub-Saharan Africa remains the deadliest region for Christians, with Islamist militant groups carrying out attacks against predominantly Christian communities, destroying churches and forcing entire populations to flee their homes.

Christians Burned Alive in Nigerian Massacre

Among the most devastating incidents was the June 13–14, 2025, attack on Yelewata, a predominantly Christian community in Nigeria’s Benue State, where more than 200 people were reportedly killed by armed militants.

According to Aid to the Church in Need, attackers set buildings ablaze, killing residents trapped inside, while approximately 3,000 survivors fled the community.

The massacre was part of a broader wave of violence across Nigeria’s Middle Belt, where Christian farming communities have faced repeated attacks involving killings, kidnappings and destruction of homes and churches.

Although disputes over land and resources contribute to the region’s instability, Christian leaders have warned that religiously motivated attacks and the failure of authorities to protect vulnerable communities have intensified the crisis.

Christian Girls Abducted and Forced Into Marriage

The persecution extends beyond mass killings.

Reports from Pakistan describe Christian girls being abducted, pressured to convert to Islam and forced into marriages, sometimes with significantly older men.

In Nigeria, women and girls captured by jihadist militants have also faced sexual violence, forced conversion and coerced marriage.

Open Doors documented 5,202 incidents involving Christians who were sexually assaulted, sexually harassed or forced to marry non-Christians during its 2026 reporting period.

Persecution Spreads Across Continents

A separate report from Aid to the Church in Need, Persecuted and Forgotten? 2024–2026, found that conditions for Christians deteriorated in 55 percent of the 18 countries examined, with no country showing an overall improvement.

The findings document different forms of persecution, including violent attacks by extremists in Africa, government restrictions on Christian worship in China, repression in North Korea and Iran, and religiously motivated violence in parts of South Asia.

Open Doors also recorded 3,632 attacks or closures involving churches and public Christian properties worldwide, while more than 224,000 Christians were forced from their homes, driven into hiding or compelled to leave their countries.

The post Nearly 5,000 Christians Killed Worldwide as New Reports Expose Massacres, Burned Churches and Forced Child Marriages appeared first on Worthy Christian News.

articles.title: South Sudan Christian Woman Reportedly Beaten To Death After Refusing Forced Marriage
articles.content:
by Stefan J. Bos, Worthy News Chief International Correspondent

JUBA (Worthy News) – Christians are mourning a young Christian woman who was reportedly beaten to death in South Sudan after refusing to marry an older Muslim man chosen by her family.

The killing reportedly took place around November 5 in Jonglei state. Advocacy group International Christian Concern (ICC) identified the 18-year-old as Ajak Mabior. In what appears to be an account of the same killing, regional broadcaster Radio Tamazuj identified her as Ajok Kelei.

“She was expected to marry an older Muslim man — a marriage she opposed because of her Christian faith and her unwillingness to be forced into it,” explained ICC.

After attempting to escape, she was reportedly killed by her own brother and cousin. Days later, police in Bor, the capital of Jonglei state, arrested the two men but released them without charges after family members demanded their freedom, arguing that “there was no case” because they were relatives, according to Christians familiar with the situation.

BOR OFFICIAL PLEDGES INVESTIGATION

Radio Tamazuj dated the killing to November 5, while the ICC gave November 6. The broadcaster reported that the family rejected the person the woman wanted to marry and chose another man for her. Its report gave no details about the intended husband’s age or religion.

Daniel Deng Panchol, the caretaker commissioner of Bor County, told Radio Tamazuj that the woman’s brother and a cousin had been arrested over the fatal beating and released without his consent. He said local authorities would investigate. It was unclear whether either suspect had since been charged.

Civil society leader Bol Deng Bol told the broadcaster that two similar cases had occurred in Jonglei the previous year.

“When a young girl is killed for refusing a forced marriage, and the killers walk free because they are family, the message is clear: Tradition is stronger than the law, and stronger than the value of a life,” a local pastor told ICC. “Many of our Christian daughters live under this same shadow.”

FORCED MARRIAGE IN SOUTH SUDAN

Human Rights Watch has documented forced marriages in Jonglei and elsewhere in South Sudan, including cases in which women and girls faced threats or violence for resisting marriages chosen by relatives. The group found that the prospect of receiving cattle or money as bride wealth could drive families to impose marriages.

South Sudan’s transitional constitution requires both people to consent freely to a marriage. The United Nations children’s agency, UNICEF, says 52 percent of girls in South Sudan marry before turning 18. The available reports give no national estimate for forced interfaith marriages.

South Sudan, where most people identify as Christian, became independent from Sudan on July 9, 2011. The split followed a 2005 peace agreement that ended a decades-long civil war and a referendum in which about 98 percent voted for independence.

About 300,000 people who had been living in northern Sudan returned south before independence, according to the World Bank.

CHRISTIANS URGE PRAYERS

After independence, Sudan moved to strip people eligible for South Sudanese citizenship of their Sudanese nationality and urged them to leave. The U.S. Commission on International Religious Freedom said most southerners living in Sudan were Christian.

In Jonglei, ICC said local Christian leaders were concerned about the danger girls face when their faith and choice of spouse conflict with family demands. The group urged churches to speak out against coercion and called on authorities to protect those at risk.

“We call on the wider Body of Christ to pray for Ajak’s justice, and for the protection of Christian girls facing forced marriages because of their faith,” an ICC staff member said.

“Pray that the church will have the courage to speak against religious coercion and violence, and that the authorities will uphold the law and protect vulnerable believers.”

The post South Sudan Christian Woman Reportedly Beaten To Death After Refusing Forced Marriage appeared first on Worthy Christian News.
